analysis.content:
# Functional Analysis — REQ-0001

Baseline: 124a4eb4597b0fdfa2fbd179ec109e5e16ec15a2127c4b4f7e7bc79de480ed0c
Approval: BD-0002
Handoff: human-business-advance-a77bda61-729f-4de7-8dec-7911fb7a8cb4

## Functional requirements
### FR-001 — Record a future due date
Business sources: B-002
Discovery evidence: D-0001
Status: specified
Questions: -
Statement: A user can assign a future due date to a task, and that task records the supplied date. This specifies an upcoming-commitment scenario; it does not establish a future-only restriction or decide past-date behavior.

### FR-002 — Keep a task without a due date
Business sources: B-002, B-003
Discovery evidence: D-0005, D-0004
Status: specified
Questions: -
Statement: A task can have no due date. Assigning a due date is optional.

### FR-003 — Past-date assignment
Business sources: B-002
Discovery evidence: D-0001
Status: blocked
Questions: AQ-001
Statement: The outcome of attempting to assign a past due date is not specified. Neither acceptance nor rejection is selected by this draft.

## Use cases
### UC-001 — Record an upcoming commitment
Business sources: B-002
Discovery evidence: D-0001
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-001
Questions: -
Actor: A user managing a task
Preconditions: A task is available for due-date assignment.
Trigger: The user wants to record the task's upcoming due date.
Main flow: 1. The user identifies the task and supplies a future due date.
  2. The task records the supplied due date.
Alternative flows: If the task is left without a due date, the optionality scenario applies. A past-date attempt has no specified outcome pending the deferred business decision.
Outcome: The task has the user-supplied future due date.

### UC-002 — Leave a task undated
Business sources: B-002, B-003
Discovery evidence: D-0005, D-0004
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-002
Questions: -
Actor: A user managing a task
Preconditions: The task has no due date.
Trigger: The user chooses not to assign a due date.
Main flow: 1. The user leaves the task without a due date.
  2. The task remains undated; a due date is not required.
Alternative flows: The user may instead assign a future due date using the assignment scenario. Removing an already assigned date is not specified by this use case.
Outcome: The task remains without a due date.

## Business rules
### BR-001 — Due dates are optional
Business sources: B-003
Discovery evidence: D-0005, D-0004
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-002
Questions: -
Statement: A task is not required to have a due date. This rule follows explicit human confirmation of the originating optionality assumption.

## Acceptance criteria
### AC-001 — Record the supplied future date
Business sources: B-002
Discovery evidence: D-0001
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-001
Questions: -
Given: A task with no assigned due date, and a future calendar date selected by the user.
When: The user assigns the selected date as that task's due date.
Then: That task has an assigned due date whose day, month and year match the selected date. Its resulting state is a task with that assigned date, rather than a task without a due date.

### AC-002 — No due date is required
Business sources: B-003
Discovery evidence: D-0005
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-002
Questions: -
Given: A task with no assigned due date.
When: The user leaves the due date unspecified for that task.
Then: That task remains without an assigned due date: there is no assigned date value. This is a permitted task state; assigning a due date is not required.

## Business coverage
- **B-001** [contextual] - | Tracking upcoming commitments provides business value; it does not introduce another functional capability.
- **B-002** [elaborated] FR-001, FR-002 | Covers assignment and optionality. Past-date behavior remains blocked separately. Reminders and notifications remain outside the initial scope.
- **B-003** [elaborated] FR-002, BR-001 | Explicitly confirmed optionality is represented as behavior and a business rule.
- **B-004** [excluded] - | Reminders are outside the initial scope; no reminder feature or artificial requirement is created.

## Inherited unresolved items
- **U-001** [D-0006] Deferred: whether users may choose a date in the past. Decision D-0007 defers this question until consultation with support. No rule allowing or rejecting past dates has been decided.

## Analysis questions
### AQ-001 — May a due date be in the past?
Business sources: B-002
Discovery evidence: D-0006
Status: deferred
Affected items: FR-003
Statement: Whether users may choose a past due date remains deferred pending consultation with support. There is no acceptance criterion choosing acceptance or rejection of such a date.

### AQ-002 — Changing or clearing an existing due date
Business sources: B-002
Discovery evidence: D-0001
Status: open
Affected items: FR-001, FR-002
Statement: The ability to change or clear an already assigned due date has not yet been defined. This remains an open Analysis question, not an implied functional capability. Neither changing nor clearing an assigned due date is specified as a functional requirement or acceptance criterion. Defining either behavior requires upstream business refinement and renewed approval.

## Analysis proposals
None recorded.

payload.content:
# Technical Design — Task Due Date Management acceptance application

Status: proposed for human review; not approved. This is an acceptance demonstrator,
not a complete personal task manager or a production deployment design.

## Approved authority and observations

Consume the exact approved and explicitly advanced Functional Analysis baseline selected
by the current handoff. Its approved Business dependency and Discovery history remain
authoritative. The original requirement is unchanged. FR-001/AC-001 specify assigning
a supplied future calendar date to an undated task; FR-002/AC-002 permit an undated task.
FR-003 remains blocked. U-001/AQ-001 and AQ-002 remain unresolved, despite acknowledgement.
No business rule for past dates or changing/clearing an assigned date is established.

Inspection: the disposable project contains requirements artifacts only. There is no
existing application, repository stack, schema or build convention to extend. Seeded
task records are demonstration fixtures satisfying the use-case precondition that a
task is available; they are not a new task-creation requirement.

## Proposed architecture

Use one local process serving a small browser UI and a same-origin JSON API. Separate:
1. Domain module: Task {id, title, dueDate: null | YYYY-MM-DD}; initial-date assignment
   and undated-task representation. Store the date as a calendar string, not an instant.
2. In-memory task repository: fixed seeded task fixtures; no database, accounts or synchronization.
3. HTTP adapter: explicit route allowlist and JSON input/output; no arbitrary filesystem access.
4. Browser adapter: list seeded tasks, clearly show an absent date, and provide a labelled
   initial future-date assignment form for undated tasks. Render returned values as text.

Request flow: browser -> same-origin API -> domain service -> in-memory repository ->
JSON result -> browser renders the persisted-in-process task state. An independent API
read must return the assigned date, so this is working application state rather than
only a client-side display change.

## Proposed technology and alternatives

Use the already installed Node.js v25.9.0, built-in HTTP modules, and plain HTML/CSS/
JavaScript. This is a local acceptance environment observation, not a production runtime
support recommendation. Avoid a frontend framework, database, runtime dependencies or
build bundler for this small scope. No runtime or package is installed at the design stage.
Use Node's built-in test runner for domain and HTTP integration checks. Propose Playwright
as a pinned development-only dependency for an actual browser UI runner, using installed
Chrome. Chrome is present; Playwright is not currently resolvable from this project.
Dependency/version resolution, browser launch and executable test commands belong to the
subsequent reviewed Plan; no browser test is claimed executed now.

Alternative: a browser-only local-storage application would be smaller but would not
exercise a real HTTP/component boundary and would add an unapproved persistence choice.
A framework/database stack adds unnecessary installation and configuration for two
approved acceptance paths. The proposed in-memory process is intentionally disposable.

## Scope boundaries and explicit technical proposals

Due-date entry is calendar-only, with strict real-calendar YYYY-MM-DD parsing; preserve
exact day/month/year through the API and UI. Invalid encoding/shape/non-calendar values
are structural input errors, not a decision about valid past dates.

Demonstrate initial assignment of future dates and tasks remaining undated. Do not add
task creation/deletion/completion, reminders/notifications, date clearing or date editing.
Once assigned, show the assigned date without edit/clear controls; this means those
capabilities are absent from the demonstrator, not prohibited by an approved product rule.

For attempts outside specified behavior (a valid past/today date or reassigning/clearing
an existing date), return an explicit not-implemented-in-this-demonstrator response,
not a business validation message claiming that past dates or edits are forbidden.
These paths have no product acceptance criteria and remain blocked/open. This technical
boundary is proposed for review; it must not be represented as resolving U-001/AQ-001,
FR-003 or AQ-002. The final report must state the application demonstrates only the
specified subset, even if its executable checks pass.

For reproducible tests, inject a reference calendar day. In the live demo, display the
server UTC reference day explicitly and use it only to identify the demonstrated future
path. No production per-user timezone or today-date policy is inferred. The UI must
identify this as an acceptance demonstration with incomplete date policies.

In-memory data resets when the process restarts. This is a proposed test-environment
limitation, not a user-approved retention requirement. No sensitive production data,
external services, network deployment or authenticated user behavior is introduced.

## Security-by-design contribution

Assets are seeded task titles/dates, local process integrity, and integrity of the test
and SDLC artifacts. Treat browser input and HTTP requests as untrusted. Bind the server
to loopback on an ephemeral port; make no internet-facing deployment claim. Use explicit
routes and fixed static assets; no path-to-file concatenation, executable input, eval,
dynamic shell or external content. Bound request sizes and validate content type, object
keys, task identity and calendar syntax; return controlled JSON errors without stack traces.

Use same-origin UI/API, reject foreign origins for mutating requests, do not enable
permissive CORS, and use proportionate response headers (nosniff and a local-content CSP).
Render untrusted text through textContent, with no untrusted HTML insertion. Do not log
request bodies or credentials. There is no authentication because this is an isolated
seeded-data local demonstration; authentication and multi-user authorization are not
claimed or silently added as product requirements. Loopback alone is not a universal
security boundary; localhost misuse and dependency risks remain review concerns.

Keep the application server away from requirements/, approval artifacts, local identity
files and test evidence. Serve only the declared public assets. Source and tests remain
within the later approved Plan paths. Playwright is development-only, pinned with a
lockfile, and reviewed before use; inspect actual dependency/advisory evidence when available.
These are proposed design controls from Security 1.0.0, not an executed Security Review,
vulnerability scan, human signoff or certification.

## Verification seams and traceability

FR-001 -> domain initial-date assignment -> JSON endpoint -> browser form -> AC-001:
assert exact selected future YYYY-MM-DD in the returned task, subsequent HTTP read and
rendered browser state. FR-002 -> nullable dueDate -> JSON null and explicit undated UI
state -> AC-002. FR-003 stays blocked; never add a test asserting acceptance or business
rejection of past dates. Tests may check that the demo reports an unsupported path as
unimplemented, but must not relabel that as the missing product rule.

Plan unit checks for calendar parsing, state mutation and optionality; integration checks
for real HTTP requests, returned/read state, structural errors and route boundaries;
and actual browser tests that open the running UI, leave a fixture undated, assign a
selected future date through its form and assert the resulting display/state. Include
appropriate security-negative checks for the proposed controls. Test scenarios and
commands will be reviewed in the Plan; generated automation and code require later human
review. This document records design intent only; no tests or implementation have run.

## Review and handoff

Architecture 1.0.0 and Security 1.0.0 instruction pins are recorded by the orchestrator.
All stack, component, environment and control choices above are proposals until explicit
human Design approval. That approval must acknowledge both unresolved business topics;
it neither resolves them nor authorizes coding. After approval, wait for separate
advancement before Implementation Planning. No assignment or next-stage work is automatic.

# Implementation Plan — Task Due Date Management PoC

Status: proposed for explicit human Plan and QA scenario approval. No application source,
package installation, generated automation or test execution is authorized by this draft.
The user's "$sdlc start" answers the preceding offer to prepare this plan; it does not
mean development-start or approval. Work remains sequential.

## Authority and fixed scope

Approved Technical Design: 97e48e3c6e0fcfdcb07373d0a2cb420bbb67f374e9599a588516765206db899d
Approved Analysis baseline: 0e0144aa03e9ef1e1db88debcbf1152a0f2443e81bfb68b26706ef5c92136598
Analysis advancement: human-working-app-analysis-advance-33dd5e96-60d2-4eb2-ad14-7de118c23927

Read these exact immutable inputs before implementation. Architecture/Security choices
were approved for the PoC. Development 1.0.0 and Testing 1.0.0 instruction pins are recorded
on this plan. Their supporting specialty outlines are not installed tools.

Implement only initial future-date assignment to an existing seeded task and permitted
undated task state. Retain all inherited uncertainty: past-date policy stays deferred,
FR-003 stays blocked, and changing/clearing assigned dates stays undefined. Neither
acknowledgement nor a passing demo check defines these missing product rules.

## Runtime and dependency proposal

Use observed Node.js v25.9.0/npm 11.12.1 with built-in HTTP and node:test; plain HTML/CSS/JS;
no production third-party package, database, account, synchronization or notifications.
Use exact development dependency playwright@1.64.1, as observed in the registry during
planning, and commit no changes. Its dependency tree/integrity will be captured by the
application package-lock.json during authorized setup. Use the already installed Chrome
156.0.8078.74 at /Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome; do not
silently download browsers or change the host runtime. This records the local acceptance
environment, not a production runtime recommendation or frozen toolchain guarantee.

After explicit development start only: create the approved package manifest and use
npm install --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund --save-dev --save-exact playwright@1.64.1,
with PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD=1. Installation is limited to this disposable
project and its lockfile/node_modules. No global install, credentials, skill installation,
external infrastructure or orchestrator edits. A dependency incompatibility/advisory or
unavailable registry/browser is a reported blocker; do not switch versions or omit checks
without the necessary plan review.

## Ordered tasks and allowed source boundaries

T-001 — Prepare the local project manifest, exact development dependency/lockfile,

T-003 — Implement the loopback HTTP server, route/static-asset allowlist and JSON adapter,

T-005 — Finish the check runner/build integrity checks and run unit/build checks through

The union of these paths is the complete application source boundary. Do not modify
requirements metadata/history/baselines directly. Do not add task CRUD/completion,
reminders, persistence, accounts or other business capabilities. A scope/design change
requires renewed upstream decisions instead of an improvised correction.

## Intended interfaces and demonstration boundary

Repository records contain id, seeded title, and dueDate null or YYYY-MM-DD. Persist only
in the running process. GET /api/tasks reads tasks; a narrowly validated JSON mutation
route performs initial future-date assignment. Static routes serve only the declared
index, stylesheet and browser script. Runtime server listens on 127.0.0.1 and an ephemeral
port; the standalone entrypoint reports its actual URL. Tests construct isolated servers.

Keep calendar strings unchanged, validating actual calendar dates without JS date rollover.
For tests inject a fixed reference day. The interactive UI displays the server's UTC
reference day as an explicit demonstration/testing convention, never a new business rule.
Use separate seeded tasks per scenario; provide an explicit undated state and initial
assignment form. After assignment show the exact date and no edit/clear controls.

A valid past/today date or an existing-date change/clear attempt receives an explicit
not-implemented-in-this-demonstrator response, with stored state unchanged. Do not label
that result "past dates forbidden" or imply a final product rule. Structural malformed
inputs, unknown IDs/routes and oversized bodies receive controlled errors. The app remains
a deliberately incomplete demonstrator of the approved acceptance subset, not a complete
To-Do product. Restarting discards task data; do not claim a retention requirement.

## QA scenarios proposed for approval before automation

TS-001 / AC-002 / FR-002 — With an undated seeded task, load the API and browser UI and
leave the date unspecified. Assert JSON dueDate is null, the UI explicitly shows no date,
and merely viewing/reloading does not assign one. No empty-date mutation is required.

TS-002 / AC-001 / FR-001 — For another undated task, select a known future calendar day,
fill the actual browser date field and submit through the real UI. Assert the displayed
day/month/year exactly match the selection, then independently read the API and reload
the UI to confirm the same in-process state. Assert the other undated task is unchanged.

TS-003 / AC-001, AC-002 — In unit tests, cover exact date preservation, absence as null,
valid calendar boundaries, impossible dates and malformed types, using an injected clock.
Cover nonexistent task identity and isolation of separate task records.

TS-004 / AC-001, AC-002 — Through real HTTP requests, verify undated and initial-assignment
results, response/content types, no hidden assignment on reads, exact readback and
controlled malformed/oversized JSON errors. Cleanly close every ephemeral server.

TS-005 / AC-001, AC-002 — Verify fixed-route/static-asset boundaries, traversal attempts,
foreign-Origin mutation rejection, request-size limits, security response headers and
safe rendering through text nodes. Check seeded titles resembling HTML/script appear as
literal text without execution, network egress or unsafe DOM insertion.

TS-006 / AC-001, AC-002 — Verify that the demonstrator identifies unsupported past/today
and reassignment/clear paths as unimplemented without silently changing state. This is
a harness boundary check only: it is NOT FR-003 coverage or a decision on AQ-001/AQ-002.
No test claims whether the final product should accept or reject a past date or allow edits.

TS-007 / AC-001, AC-002 — Inspect the exact locked development dependency tree with npm
audit, preserving actual registry output and exit status. Report advisory or availability
failures honestly; they are not passes and must not be bypassed to progress.

## Named deterministic checks

C-UNIT (unit): node scripts/check.mjs unit. Execute node:test domain tests (TS-003),
using isolated fixtures and clock, and retain real exit/output. No server/browser run.
C-BUILD (build): node scripts/check.mjs build. Syntax-check all declared JS/MJS source and
runners, verify static assets/import references and package/lock consistency; no bundler,
HTTP verification or browser launch is implied by the build result.
C-INTEGRATION (integration): node scripts/check.mjs integration. Execute actual HTTP
integration and security-negative scenarios TS-001, TS-002, TS-004, TS-005, TS-006.
C-DEPENDENCIES (integration): node scripts/check.mjs dependencies. Run npm audit --json
with the project lockfile and preserve actual results, including dev dependencies.
Nonzero audit/network errors remain failures, with no suppression or claimed clean scan.
C-UI (ui): node scripts/check.mjs ui. Launch installed Chrome through pinned Playwright,
start the real loopback application, navigate and exercise actual form interactions
TS-001/TS-002 and applicable TS-005/TS-006. Assert meaningful browser outcomes, not only
HTTP status or a screenshot. Browser launch failure is not a pass.

Only C-UNIT/C-BUILD execute in Development. After the human reviews actual code and
new automation, explicitly approves the exact implementation/source and separately
advances, execute C-INTEGRATION, C-DEPENDENCIES and C-UI sequentially in Verification.
A passing process exit is not a substitute for assertion quality; inspect actual results.

## Execution evidence and security review

All named checks use literal argv, cwd '.', per-check deadlines and no generated shell.
Record tool versions, scenario/requirement IDs, actual status, exit/output and source
fingerprint through check-run. Test outputs must not modify hashed source inputs.
Only test runners (never the application server) may additionally write fresh, uniquely
named output under this Epic's test-evidence/ directory. Store UI screenshots, browser
trace, check reports and their checksums there; print relative evidence paths and hashes
into captured stdout so the immutable check record references the actual retained files.
Never overwrite prior evidence, metadata or baselines. Browser profiles/caches may use
system temporary directories and must be cleaned up. No app server serves requirements/
or test-evidence/. No implementation is permitted in the orchestrator checkout.

After Verification, wait for separate advancement to Security Review. Use Security
instructions to inspect the current source and real test/advisory evidence: input/route
controls, XSS/origin handling, dependency exposure, secrets and unnecessary capabilities.
Record findings and limitations with source/requirement links; no certification claim.
Any finding requires explicit remediation authorization. Fix only within this plan,
retain failing evidence, rerun checks, obtain fresh human code/automation approval, and
repeat Verification/Security as required. Changing the dependency or scope beyond the
approved pin requires corresponding renewed approval, not an automatic install upgrade.

Final report binds exact Analysis/Design/Plan, source fingerprint, actual named check
results and browser evidence, Security report and unresolved business items. Finalization
and every stage advancement require separate human authorization. A report of this
specified subset is neither full product completeness nor release/deployment approval.
